parsed.explanation: Lemma 4.1 proves existence of an ordering with nested absolute difference g, whereas v(B) was defined using the decreasing ordering. These are not equivalent because nested absolute difference is order-dependent. The witness verifies this: decreasing order 8,7,6,5,4 gives value 4, while 8,6,5,7,4 gives 0. Indeed P={8,7} and N={6,5,4} have equal sums, so this also directly exposes the analogous gap in the g=0 branch of Theorem 4.2. The later strategy explicitly processes b_1≥⋯≥b_r and therefore requires the unproved decreasing-order bound. No argument elsewhere repairs this mismatch, so the all-n upper bound is incomplete as written.
